name: Leviathan
description: A colossal sea serpent of biblical legend, basically the ocean's version of a boss fight.

name: Satyr
description: Half-man, half-goat, full-time party animal with a penchant for pan flutes and poor decisions.

name: Nymph
description: Nature spirits that embody the beauty of forests, rivers, and fields—like Mother Nature's influencers.

name: Anansi
description: A clever spider-trickster from African folklore who spins both webs and stories.

name: Bunyip
description: A mysterious Australian swamp creature—think cryptid meets cautionary tale.

name: Iktomi
description: A Lakota spider-trickster god who weaves chaos with intelligence and mischief.

name: Loch Ness Monster
description: Scotland's most elusive lake dweller—photogenic, yet camera shy.

name: Chupacabra
description: The goat-sucker of Latin American lore, feared by livestock and embraced by late-night TV.

name: Jackalope
description: A mythical horned rabbit—equal parts adorable and armed.

name: Phoenix
description: A firebird that bursts into flames and rises from the ashes. Ultimate glow-up.

name: Griffin
description: The majestic fusion of lion and eagle—basically nature's power couple.

name: Minotaur
description: Bull-headed maze dweller with anger management issues.

name: Cerberus
description: The three-headed hound guarding the gates of the Underworld—think security with bite.

name: Hydra
description: Cut off one head, two more grow—medieval multitasking nightmare.

name: Cyclops
description: A one-eyed giant with a terrible depth perception and worse manners.

name: Chimera
description: A fiery mashup of lion, goat, and snake—ancient Greece's version of a patch update gone rogue.

name: Sphinx
description: Riddle-loving guardian with the body of a lion and the face of a trivia night champion.

name: Kraken
description: Giant sea monster with a flair for dramatic ship-smashing entrances.

name: Banshee
description: A wailing Irish spirit—when she screams, someone's about to get ghosted. Literally.

name: Centaur
description: Half-man, half-horse, all gallop. Known for archery and identity confusion.

name: Pegasus
description: A winged horse who makes a dramatic entrance look like child's play.

name: Basilisk
description: Deadly reptile that can kill with a glare—basically a toxic gaze personified.

name: Gorgon
description: Snake-haired women whose gaze turns folks to stone. Zero tolerance for awkward stares.

name: Harpy
description: Winged women of vengeance and shrieking doom. Not your ideal dinner guests.

name: Siren
description: Sea-dwelling singers whose songs spell doom. Basically ancient Spotify with bad intentions.

name: Djinn
description: Magical beings with big powers and even bigger fine print.

name: Kitsune
description: Shapeshifting fox spirit of Japanese lore, equally known for wisdom and mischief.

name: Wendigo
description: Cannibal spirit of the frozen north, driven by hunger and spooky winter vibes.

name: Kappa
description: A polite yet dangerous river creature from Japan—just bow back and you'll be fine.

name: Naga
description: Serpent beings from Hindu and Buddhist mythology—divine and deadly.

name: Thunderbird
description: Giant bird of Native American lore that brings the storm—and the thunder.

name: Manticore
description: Lion body, scorpion tail, human face—nature's uncanny collage.

name: Yeti
description: Himalayan snow monster. Cold, elusive, and probably tired of the paparazzi.

name: Upyr
description: A Slavic vampire who snacks during the day. A real overachiever in the undead community.

name: Chort
description: A demon of Slavic folklore—goat horns, evil laugh, and chaotic energy.

name: Baba Yaga
description: Witch of the woods who flies in a mortar and pestle—your grandma if she were an eldritch boss.
